# Sirach Chapter 13 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 13 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_013_page_001.jpg

---

**13:1** Whoever touches pitch will be defiled, and whoever associates with a proud man will become like him.

**13:2** Do not lift a burden too heavy for you, and do not associate with one mightier and richer than you. What fellowship has a clay pot with an iron kettle? This one strikes, and that one is shattered.

**13:3** A rich man does wrong and even adds threats; a poor man is wronged and even must beg forgiveness.

**13:4** If you are useful he will make use of you, but if you become weak he will abandon you.

**13:5** If you have anything, he will live with you; he will drain you, and he will not feel sorry.

**13:6** Does he need you? He will deceive you, he will smile at you and give you hope; he will speak graciously to you and say, "What do you need?"

**13:7** He will shame you at his feasts until he has drained you twice or three times over, and at the end he will mock you; afterward, when he sees you, he will forsake you, and will shake his head at you.

**13:8** Take heed not to be led astray, and not to be humiliated in your moment of pleasure.

**13:9** When a powerful man invites you, decline; and so much the more he will invite you.

**13:10** Do not push forward, lest you be thrust back; and do not stand at a distance, lest you be forgotten.

**13:11** Do not hold yourself as equal with him, and do not trust his abundance of words; for by much talking he will test you, and while smiling he will be examining you.

**13:12** One who shows no mercy is one who does not guard his words; he will not spare you from pain or from chains.

**13:13** Take heed and be very careful, for you are walking with the fall of yourself. When you hear these things, wake up in your sleep.

**13:14** Love the Lord all your life, and call upon him for your salvation.

**13:15** Every creature loves its own kind, and every person his neighbor.

**13:16** All flesh associates with those of its own kind, and a man cleaves to one like himself.

**13:17** What fellowship does a wolf have with a lamb? No more does a sinner have with a devout man.

**13:18** What peace is there between a hyena and a dog? And what peace between a rich man and a poor man?

**13:19** Wild donkeys in the desert are the prey of lions; likewise, poor men are the pasture of the rich.

**13:20** Lowliness is an abomination to the proud; likewise, a poor man is an abomination to the rich.

**13:21** When a rich man stumbles, he is supported by his friends; but when the humble man falls, he is pushed away even by his friends.

**13:22** When the rich man trips, there are many to help him up; he says something unseemly and men justify him. The humble man trips, and they rebuke him as well; he speaks wisely and no room is made for him.

**13:23** The rich man speaks and all are silent, and they extol his words to the clouds. The poor man speaks and they say, "Who is this?" And if he stumbles, they will push him down further.

**13:24** Wealth is good if it has no sin attached to it; poverty is evil in the reckoning of the ungodly.

**13:25** The heart of a man changes his face, whether for good or for evil.

**13:26** A face that reflects a glad heart is a good sign; the search for wise sayings is a toilsome labor.
